title: Unit
description: What a measure is counted in. Free text on the KPI until 2026-09-29, and free text shows what that cost: "percent" many times over beside "score", "index", "count", "USD", "rate" and "hours", no two checkable against each other. A kind rather than an enum, because every organisation measures something nobody anticipated and a closed list sends that number into a note; the standard units ship with a vault and an instance declares its own beside them, so a custom unit is not a special case. See TAXONOMY.md D10.

name.description: What this unit is called, as it reads beside a number.

symbol.description: The short form, where there is one: % for percent, hrs for hours. Optional, because most units are written out.

dimension.description: What kind of quantity this is, from the set KeyResult.kind already uses, so the two places Cartograph talks about measurement agree. What a unit is called and what it is are separate: hours and days are both durations, and something adding two measures can tell whether it may.

description.description: What exactly is counted, where the name alone could be read two ways.
